gaz.royal.alhambra.attestation_note: The mapped entity represents the palatine city within its walls.
gaz.royal.alhambra.survival_note: The enclosure, architecture and landscape survive with multiple phases.

gaz.royal.generalife.date_note: Medieval etymology and name transmitted in later accounts
gaz.royal.generalife.attestation_note: There are variants of the exact historical form of the name.
gaz.royal.generalife.survival_note: The palace, cultivated plots and water system survive with alterations.

gaz.gate.elvira.date_note: Medieval name transmitted through Arabic and Christian sources
gaz.gate.elvira.attestation_note: The identification and continuity of the place name are secure.
gaz.gate.elvira.survival_note: The main arch survives, but not the entire defensive complex.
gaz.gate.elvira.notes: Junction between enclosures and an urban axis.

gaz.gate.alhambra-arms.attestation_note: The identification of the monument is well established.
gaz.gate.alhambra-arms.notes: Northern entrance to the palatine city.

gaz.gate.alhambra-justice.date_note: Inscription and Nasrid tradition from the fourteenth century
gaz.gate.alhambra-justice.attestation_note: The name and identification of the monument are secure.

gaz.commerce.corral-carbon.date_note: Arabic name transmitted through historical scholarship
gaz.commerce.corral-carbon.attestation_note: The present name is later; its identity as a Nasrid funduq is secure.
gaz.commerce.corral-carbon.survival_note: The building survives with restorations and alterations.

gaz.civic.maristan.survival_note: Remains and an archaeological plot survive, with later reconstructions.

gaz.water.banuelo.date_note: Transmitted Arabic name with debated chronology
gaz.water.banuelo.attestation_note: Its identity as a medieval hammam is secure.
gaz.water.banuelo.survival_note: The medieval bath survives with restorations.

gaz.urban.albaicin.date_note: Historical name with long continuity, applied here to the large urban sector
gaz.urban.albaicin.attestation_note: It groups several nuclei and suburbs, rather than a single homogeneous unit.
gaz.urban.albaicin.survival_note: Topography, the urban fabric and numerous elements survive, with alterations.
gaz.urban.albaicin.notes: Geometric derivation from three adjoining enclosures. The outer edge retains the audited Nasrid wall, and the inner edges are checked against Mapa 5 and the PEPRI. It does not correspond to the present administrative neighbourhood.

gaz.urban.lower-medina.date_note: Modern category based on the historical medina
gaz.urban.lower-medina.attestation_note: The qualifier ‘lower’ is analytical; the later enclosure includes incorporated suburbs.
gaz.urban.lower-medina.survival_note: Streets, plots and monuments survive, but the wall is highly fragmented.
gaz.urban.lower-medina.notes: The northern edge is revised together with the Albaicín enclosures, replacing the artificial closure along Calle Elvira. The southern outer perimeter retains the previous archaeological reconstruction. This entity combines the medina and its incorporated suburbs; it does not claim that they all formed a single neighbourhood.
